title: Diag context payload schema (draft) — Incident Bot v2 + Console cards
content:
Draft scope
- This doc defines the JSON payload contract produced by the diagnostics aggregator and consumed by:
  (1) incident-bot v2 Slack rendering (context “cards”), and
  (2) Console deep links (dashboards, traces/logs).
- Emphasis: bounded queries, tenant-safe output, graceful degradation.

Goals
- Standardize “first 5 minutes” incident context across common incident classes:
  - Deploy regressions (recent rollout + canary)
  - Misconfig / policy changes (config diff w/ redaction)
  - Saturation / regional capacity (GPU util, queue depth, KV cache pressure, scheduler/backpressure)
- Make bot output predictable and comparable across incidents (“context completeness” scoring).
- Keep schema forward-compatible for new cards and fields.

Non-goals
- This is not the complete incident timeline schema (postmortem/timeline export is separate).
- This does not define the internal storage model for config history / deploy registry.

------------------------------
1) Envelope (top-level)

All payloads MUST be valid JSON and MUST include the “envelope” fields below. Consumers should ignore unknown fields.

Required envelope fields
- schema_version: string (SemVer; see Versioning section)
- generated_at: string (RFC3339 UTC timestamp)
- request_id: string (idempotency + debugging)
- incident:
  - incident_id: string (internal incident id if present; otherwise thread_ts)
  - slack:
    - channel_id: string
    - thread_ts: string
  - severity: string ("sev0" | "sev1" | "sev2" | "sev3" | "unknown")
  - environment: string ("prod" | "staging" | "dev" | "unknown")
- subject:
  - service: string (canonical service name; ex: "hosted-api" / "router" / "scheduler")
  - region: string (cloud region; ex: "us-east" / "eu-west"; "global" allowed)

Optional envelope fields
- subject:
  - route: string (API route if known; ex: "/v1/chat/completions")
  - pool: string (capacity pool name; ex: "hosted-gpu-a10" / "dedicated:tenant-123")
  - model: string (model id; ex: "llama-3.1-70b-instruct")
  - tenant:
    - tenant_ref: string (safe reference; see Tenant handling)
- time_window:
  - start_at: string (RFC3339)
  - end_at: string (RFC3339)
  - duration_s: number encoded as string (ex: "1800")
- completeness:
  - score: string ("0"–"100")
  - missing: array of strings (card ids missing)
  - notes: string
- degraded_mode:
  - enabled: string ("true" | "false")
  - reason: string (timeouts, upstream unhealthy, rate limited, etc.)

Tenant handling (IMPORTANT)
- Payloads can be generated in two modes:
  A) tenant-agnostic: tenant_ref omitted, metrics aggregated at service/region/pool granularity
  B) tenant-aware (privileged): tenant_ref present, but MUST be rendered as a safe reference:
     - tenant_ref format: "t/<opaque_id>" (no customer name, no email domains)
     - avoid any raw customer identifiers unless explicitly allowed by Security.

------------------------------
2) Cards array

The envelope includes a list of “cards”. Each card is independently renderable in Slack.

Top-level card list field
- cards: array of card objects

Required fields per card
- card_id: string (stable id; ex: "recent_deploys", "config_diff", "saturation", "error_budget_burn")
- card_version: string (SemVer; card-specific)
- title: string (short; Slack header)
- summary: string (<= ~500 chars; what changed / what to look at)
- status: string ("ok" | "info" | "warning" | "critical" | "unknown")
- generated_at: string (RFC3339 UTC)
- sources: array of strings (human-readable source names; ex: "Deploy Registry", "Config Service", "Metrics (Prometheus)" )

Optional fields per card
- fields: array of strings (rendered “facts”; see formatting guidance)
- links: array of strings (rendered deep links; see deep link format)
- actions: array of strings (Slack interactive action descriptors; see Actions)
- errors: array of strings (sanitized errors)
- debug: string (non-sensitive debug hint; safe to show in Slack)
- redaction:
  - applied: string ("true" | "false")
  - policy: string (policy version id)
  - notes: string

Formatting guidance for “fields”
- Each entry is a single line of text, optimized for Slack blocks, e.g.:
  - "Canary: FAIL (p95 +38%, 5xx +2.1%)"
  - "Rollout phase: 25% → 50% (in progress)"
  - "GPU util (p95): 96% (threshold: 92%)"
- Use consistent units and percent formatting. Prefer p50/p95 and max depending on signal.

------------------------------
3) Card definitions (v0.1)

3.1 recent_deploys card
Purpose: correlate symptoms with recent rollouts. Should be fast and always attemptable.

Card-specific recommended fields
- "Last deploy: <service>@<version> (<sha>) <age> ago"
- "Rollout: <phase> (<percent>), canary: <PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN>"
- "Changed components: <router/scheduler/runtime/etc>" (if multi-service)
- "Related PRs: <links>" (prefer 1–3 links; truncate)

Minimum viable links
- "Deploy timeline (Console): <url>"
- "Commit/PR: <url>"

Notes
- Represent partial propagation explicitly (avoid implying a deploy is global).
- If service mapping is uncertain, set status=unknown and include debug hint (no raw internal ids).

3.2 config_diff card
Purpose: show what changed in routing/policy/feature flags/quota/model pins, safely.

Card-specific requirements
- Always indicate redaction policy + that content is tenant-safe.
- Highlight only allowlisted keys by default.

Recommended fields
- "Config scope: <service/route/region/pool/tenant_ref>"
- "Change window: <t0> → <t1>"
- "Top changes (allowlisted):"
  - "+ routing.fallback_enabled: false → true"
  - "~ quotas.rpm_limit: 6000 → 3000"
  - "~ model.pin: llama-3.1-70b → llama-3.1-8b"
- "Redacted items: <count> (use modal to view safe preview)"

Links
- "Open config diff (Console): <url>" (preferred)
- "Runbook: config diff debugging: <url>" (internal)

3.3 saturation card
Purpose: quickly answer “are we saturated and where?” across GPU, queueing, KV cache, scheduler.

Recommended fields
- "GPU util (p95): <x>% (thr <y>%)"
- "Queue depth (p95): <x> (thr <y>)"
- "KV cache pressure: <x>% evictions: <rate>"
- "Backpressure/admission: <state> (drops: <rate>)"
- "Capacity: <available>/<total> (regional)"

Links
- "Saturation overview dashboard: <url>"
- "Scheduler dashboard: <url>"
- "Trace sample (latest 15m): <url>" (only if low-cost)

3.4 error_budget_burn card
Purpose: unify “how bad is this?” with immediate SLO burn context.

Recommended fields
- "SLO: <name> — burn 1h: <x>x, burn 6h: <y>x"
- "Errors: 5xx <rate>, timeouts <rate>, streaming disconnects <rate>"

Links
- "Error budget burn: <url>"
- "Service latency dashboard: <url>"

3.5 (Optional) notes card
Purpose: a safe place for the bot to post “manual steps” when degraded.

Recommended fields
- "Live queries degraded: using cached context from <timestamp>"
- "Manual commands: /diag deploys <service> <region> ; /diag saturation <service>"

------------------------------
4) Redaction + data safety

Hard rules
- Never include secrets, tokens, private keys, raw auth headers, or customer PII.
- All config diffs MUST pass through redaction BEFORE entering the payload.
- Telemetry must be bounded and label-cardinality-controlled; avoid tenant identifiers in metric labels.

Redaction policy (draft)
- Two-layer approach:
  1) Key-based allowlist: Only emit values for explicitly allowlisted config paths.
     - Example allowlist (not exhaustive):
       - routing.* (but exclude routing.credentials*, routing.headers*)
       - feature_flags.* (values ok, but redact any "targeting" rules that contain emails/domains)
       - quotas.* (numeric ok)
       - model.* (ids ok)
       - rollouts.* (phase/percent ok)
  2) Value-based secret detection: pattern match & heuristic scanning.
     - If a value matches secret-like patterns, replace with "<redacted>" and increment redacted_count.

Patterns to redact (examples)
- Any value matching:
  - "(?i)api[_-]?key"
  - "(?i)secret"
  - "(?i)token"
  - "(?i)password"
  - JWT-like: "eyJ[0-9A-Za-z_-]{10,}\.eyJ[0-9A-Za-z_-]{10,}\.[0-9A-Za-z_-]{10,}"
  - Private key headers: "-----BEGIN (RSA |EC |OPENSSH )?PRIVATE KEY-----"
- Any value with high entropy heuristic (TBD thresholds) should be redacted conservatively.

Rendering redaction UX
- Slack cards should never attempt to “reveal” redacted values.
- Slack should display:
  - “Redaction applied (policy <id>). <n> items redacted.”
  - Provide Console deep link for authorized viewers (Console will enforce authz again).

Audit + access (schema hooks)
- When privileged mode is used (tenant-aware metrics or expanded diffs), include:
  - card.redaction.policy
  - card.debug = "audit_event_emitted" (do not include event ids in Slack)

------------------------------
5) Deep link format

All links should be pre-parameterized to the incident window and subject.

Link guidelines
- Always include a time window (start/end or “last N minutes”), region, service.
- Prefer Console links over raw metrics explorer links.
- Keep URLs short when possible; use a short-link service if available.

Recommended link labels
- "Console — Deploy timeline"
- "Console — Config diff"
- "Console — Saturation"
- "Console — Error budget burn"
- "Tracing — Sample traces"
- "Logs — Correlated logs"

------------------------------
6) Boundedness + failure behavior

Performance budgets (draft targets)
- Bot initial response card set: p95 < 3s (cached) / < 8s (uncached)
- Any single upstream call: timeout <= 2s (telemetry), <= 3s (deploy/config)
- Total upstream calls per incident thread interaction: <= 8 (coalesced)

Schema support for degraded mode
- envelope.degraded_mode.enabled=true indicates the card set may be incomplete or cached.
- Cards should include errors[] with user-actionable next steps, not stack traces.

Error sanitization
- errors[] is user-visible; do not include internal hostnames, SQL, raw query strings with sensitive labels.

------------------------------
7) Versioning + compatibility

schema_version (envelope)
- Use SemVer: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
  - MAJOR: breaking changes (rename/remove fields, meaning changes)
  - MINOR: additive fields or new cards
  - PATCH: clarifications / doc changes (should not change runtime expectations)

card_version (per card)
- Cards evolve independently. Consumers should render unknown fields as text-only fallback.

Compatibility rules
- Producers MUST remain backward compatible with previous MINOR versions for at least 60 days (TBD) after GA.
- Consumers MUST:
  - ignore unknown fields
  - handle missing optional fields
  - treat unknown card_id as "Custom" and render title/summary/links only

Deprecation practice
- Add "deprecated:" note in the card summary (short) and track removal date in changelog (out of band).

------------------------------
8) Example payload (illustrative)

{
  "schema_version": "0.1.0",
  "generated_at": "2025-03-06T19:22:11Z",
  "request_id": "diag_01HXYZ...",
  "incident": {
    "incident_id": "inc_2025_03_06_042",
    "slack": {"channel_id": "C012AB3CD", "thread_ts": "1741288901.123"},
    "severity": "sev1",
    "environment": "prod"
  },
  "subject": {"service": "hosted-api", "region": "eu-west", "route": "/v1/chat/completions"},
  "time_window": {"start_at": "2025-03-06T19:00:00Z", "end_at": "2025-03-06T19:22:00Z", "duration_s": "1320"},
  "completeness": {"score": "85", "missing": ["config_diff"], "notes": "config service timeout"},
  "degraded_mode": {"enabled": "true", "reason": "config_diff upstream timeout; saturation from cache"},
  "cards": [
    {
      "card_id": "recent_deploys",
      "card_version": "0.1.0",
      "title": "Recent deploys",
      "summary": "Deploy to hosted-api started 18m ago; canary failing on 5xx.",
      "status": "critical",
      "generated_at": "2025-03-06T19:22:10Z",
      "sources": ["Deploy Registry"],
      "fields": [
        "Last deploy: hosted-api@2025.03.06.1 (sha 9f2c1d3) 18m ago",
        "Rollout phase: 25% (in progress)",
        "Canary: FAIL (5xx +1.9%, p95 +31%)"
      ],
      "links": [
        "Console — Deploy timeline: https://console.redwood.example/deploys?svc=hosted-api®ion=eu-west&from=...&to=...",
        "PR/Commit: https://github.com/redwood/incident-bot/pull/1842"
      ]
    },
    {
      "card_id": "saturation",
      "card_version": "0.1.0",
      "title": "Saturation signals",
      "summary": "GPU and queue depth elevated in eu-west; likely capacity/scheduler pressure.",
      "status": "warning",
      "generated_at": "2025-03-06T19:22:11Z",
      "sources": ["Metrics (Prometheus)", "Scheduler metrics"],
      "fields": [
        "GPU util (p95): 96% (thr 92%)",
        "Queue depth (p95): 410 (thr 250)",
        "KV cache pressure: 88% (evictions: 12/s)",
        "Backpressure: ON (drops: 0.7%)"
      ],
      "links": [
        "Console — Saturation: https://console.redwood.example/dashboards/saturation?svc=hosted-api®ion=eu-west&from=...&to=..."
      ]
    },
    {
      "card_id": "error_budget_burn",
      "card_version": "0.1.0",
      "title": "SLO / error budget burn",
      "summary": "5xx SLO burning fast in eu-west.",
      "status": "critical",
      "generated_at": "2025-03-06T19:22:11Z",
      "sources": ["SLO Toolkit"],
      "fields": [
        "SLO: hosted-api 5xx — burn 1h: 14.2x, burn 6h: 5.1x"
      ],
      "links": [
        "Console — Error budget burn: https://console.redwood.example/slo/burn?svc=hosted-api®ion=eu-west&from=...&to=..."
      ]
    },
    {
      "card_id": "notes",
      "card_version": "0.1.0",
      "title": "Diagnostics notes",
      "summary": "Config diff unavailable (timeout). Try again or use Console link.",
      "status": "info",
      "generated_at": "2025-03-06T19:22:11Z",
      "sources": ["Diagnostics Aggregator"],
      "fields": [
        "Live config diff query timed out after 3s",
        "Next: /diag config-diff hosted-api eu-west (retries with backoff)"
      ]
    }
  ]
}

------------------------------
9) Validation + testing (producer requirements)

Producer must enforce
- Maximum payload size (Slack constraints + safety): target <= 45KB, hard cap 90KB (TBD).
- Truncation rules:
  - fields: max 12 lines per card by default; additional via modal/pagination
  - links: max 5 per card
  - errors: max 3 per card
- Deterministic ordering:
  - Cards in a consistent order: recent_deploys, config_diff, saturation, error_budget_burn, notes

Suggested unit tests
- Redaction tests:
  - known secret patterns are redacted
  - non-secret numeric/quota fields remain
- Schema compat tests:
  - unknown card_id does not break rendering
- Bounded query tests:
  - query count, timeout behavior, caching flags

------------------------------
10) Open questions / TODO

- Tenant-aware mode: what exact conditions enable it (Sev0/Sev1 only + break-glass?) and how do we represent that state safely in the payload?
- Should completeness.score be computed by producer (preferred for consistency) or by bot consumer?
- Do we need a separate “trace_samples” card, or is it a set of links on saturation/error_budget cards?
- Finalize allowlist paths for config diff (need Security + Platform sign-off).
- Confirm link base domains and whether we require short-links in Slack.

Changelog
- 2025-02-18: Initial draft skeleton (envelope + card model).
- 2025-02-27: Added redaction policy notes + degraded_mode.
- 2025-03-06: Added saturation/error_budget card guidance + example payload.
